title: Police seize Rs 1.03 crore in cash from Trinamool office in Diamond Harbour
dek: Police say the raid in Sarisha followed the questioning of Abhishek Banerjee's arrested aide, and that the cash may be linked to an illegal soil-mining case. Who the money belongs to is still unclear.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Police in South 24 Parganas have seized Rs 1,02,79,000 in cash, just over Rs 1 crore, from a Trinamool Congress party office in Sarisha in the Diamond Harbour block, a senior officer said on Wednesday. Police say the raid followed the questioning of Sumit Roy, an arrested personal assistant of Trinamool general secretary and Diamond Harbour MP Abhishek Banerjee.

Abhishek Majumdar, Additional Superintendent of Police (zonal) of the Diamond Harbour police district, told a press conference that the cash may be linked to a case of illegal soil excavation registered at Kalitala police station, one report said. He said investigators were examining where the money came from, who it belonged to and why it was being kept there. Police have not said that anyone has been charged over the cash.

## Whose office

The officer identified the premises as the office of Shamim Ahmed, the Magrahat West MLA, according to one report, which described Ahmed as a rebel Trinamool MLA. Ahmed did not respond to reporters' queries about the seizure. Speaking to a Bengali news site, Majumdar said: "Whose party office it is, is being investigated. But it was a Trinamool office."

The Trinamool Congress said the building had been leased by the party for three years from 2023, one report said. It said the office was vandalised and looted on the night of 21 May, that a police complaint was filed, and that the building was then handed back to its owner. The party's account suggests it no longer used the premises; police have not responded to that point publicly.

Reports differ on the timing of the raid: some said it took place on Wednesday, while one reported that it was carried out on Tuesday night.

## The soil-mining case

According to police, soil was illegally dug and sold from a plot in the Kalitala area between 2017 and 2025. One report said that police estimate its market value at about Rs 300 crore and say the proceeds reached several people, including some described as influential. Police suspect, but have not established, a link between that case and the cash.

Sumit Roy was arrested on 31 October in the soil-theft case, one report said. Another report said that he had earlier been named and arrested in a land case in Salboni, Paschim Medinipur, and was in judicial custody before police took him into custody in the soil case on Saturday.

## Background

The seizure is the latest turn in a series of investigations into Trinamool leaders since the BJP took power in Bengal in May, with Suvendu Adhikari as Chief Minister. Abhishek Banerjee has accused investigating agencies of leaking details of the cases against him to the media, and on Tuesday the Supreme Court asked the Calcutta High Court to hear his plea for interim relief when it reopens on 16 November. Adhikari said last week that a former aide of Banerjee who had been questioned by police "seems to have disclosed everything".

Banerjee has not commented publicly on the seizure, and no statement from the BJP on it had been reported by Wednesday evening.

## What happens next

Police say they are tracing the source of the money and the financial records linked to it, and that Roy is being questioned further about the transactions. Any charges arising from the seizure would be filed in court; none had been announced by Wednesday evening.
